findings.body: Two encoders are constructed, written to, and immediately discarded on every ECDSA sign conversion; the dead statements confuse readers into thinking they contribute to the returned DER value and add pointless allocations.
findings.failure_mode: Dead code performing useless work and reducing readability of the security-sensitive encoding path.
findings.impact: Two encoders are constructed, written to, and immediately discarded on every ECDSA sign conversion; the dead statements confuse readers into thinking they contribute to the returned DER value and add pointless allocations.
findings.root_cause: Leftover statements from refactoring were not removed before the final writeDerSeq expression.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the two unused `ASN1Encoder.create().write(...)` statements; the subsequent writeDerSeq call already performs the actual encoding.
findings.title: Dead ASN1Encoder instances created and discarded in concatenatedRSToASN1DER
findings.trigger: Every invocation of concatenatedRSToASN1DER executes these two statements whose ASN1Encoder results are never used.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch lines 114-115 show `ASN1Encoder.create().write(rBigInteger);` and `ASN1Encoder.create().write(sBigInteger);` whose return values are discarded. Lines 117-121 create fresh encoders for the actual `writeDerSeq` call. These two statements perform allocations and writes that contribute nothing to the returned DER value - classic dead code from incomplete refactoring.

pr.body:
…tory

closes #33831

This is the Keycloak main part for solving the https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 and adding the related changes in the authz-client on the Keycloak side, which can then be later synced to the keycloak-client repository. 

In the end, I am using approach (2) from https://github.com/keycloak/keycloak/issues/32962 with adding the method `order()` to `CryptoProvider`, which allows to have multiple instances of `CryptoProvider` on classpath (Keycloak testsuite still uses the `DefaultCryptoProvider` as before this PR).

raw_findings.body: Source compilation of external implementations fails, and pre-compiled implementations discovered via ServiceLoader throw AbstractMethodError when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during sorting, breaking crypto initialization entirely.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Existing CryptoProvider implementations fail to compile or throw AbstractMethodError during provider detection.
raw_findings.impact: Source compilation of external implementations fails, and pre-compiled implementations discovered via ServiceLoader throw AbstractMethodError when `CryptoIntegration.detectProvider` calls `CryptoProvider::order` during sorting, breaking crypto initialization entirely.
raw_findings.root_cause: An abstract method was added to a published SPI interface instead of a default method.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Declare the method with a default implementation, e.g. `default int order() { return 100; }`, so existing CryptoProvider implementations remain binary and source compatible.
raw_findings.title: New abstract `order()` method on public CryptoProvider interface breaks existing external implementations
raw_findings.trigger: Any third-party or out-of-tree class implementing the public `org.keycloak.common.crypto.CryptoProvider` interface is compiled against the old interface or loaded at runtime after this change without being updated.

raw_findings.body: Previously this misconfiguration failed fast with an IllegalStateException; now the winner among equal-order providers is decided by ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order and only logged at debug level, so a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS DefaultCryptoProvider.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Nondeterministic, silently logged selection of the active crypto provider in previously fail-fast misconfigurations, potentially bypassing FIPS crypto.
raw_findings.impact: Previously this misconfiguration failed fast with an IllegalStateException; now the winner among equal-order providers is decided by ServiceLoader/classpath iteration order and only logged at debug level, so a FIPS deployment can silently run with the non-FIPS DefaultCryptoProvider.
raw_findings.root_cause: The multiple-provider guard was replaced by order-based sorting without any tie-breaking or escalation when orders are equal.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: When the two highest-priority providers report the same order value, keep throwing IllegalStateException (or at minimum log the ignored providers at WARN), so ties between full providers are not resolved nondeterministically and silently.
raw_findings.title: Removed multiple-provider fail-fast allows silent nondeterministic provider selection when orders tie
raw_findings.trigger: Two full providers with equal order values (DefaultCryptoProvider, WildFlyElytronProvider and FIPS1402Provider all return 200) end up on the same classpath, e.g. a misconfigured deployment shipping both the default and FIPS crypto jars.

raw_findings.body: readInteger calls read(-1) which allocates `new byte[-1]` and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException, and readNext computes a wrong slice length, instead of the declared IOException, so callers catching IOException see an unexpected runtime exception.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Unchecked NegativeArraySizeException or silent misparse on non-DER input instead of the contracted IOException.
raw_findings.impact: readInteger calls read(-1) which allocates `new byte[-1]` and throws an unchecked NegativeArraySizeException, and readNext computes a wrong slice length, instead of the declared IOException, so callers catching IOException see an unexpected runtime exception.
raw_findings.root_cause: readLength preserves BouncyCastle's -1 indefinite-length sentinel, but none of the new callers (readSequence, readInteger, readNext) check for it.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: In readLength, throw an IOException for the 0x80 indefinite-length octet (invalid in DER) instead of returning -1, or have readSequence/readInteger/readNext explicitly reject a negative length.
raw_findings.title: ASN1Decoder returns -1 sentinel for indefinite length that callers never handle
raw_findings.trigger: A malformed or attacker-shaped DER signature passed to asn1derToConcatenatedRS contains an indefinite-length octet (0x80), e.g. a BER-encoded INTEGER or SEQUENCE.

raw_findings.body: The truncation branch of integerToBytes (qLength < bytes.length) and full-size 384/521-bit r/s handling in the new ASN.1 code are never exercised; a defect specific to large-curve signatures (e.g. the ES512 66-byte length or long-form DER lengths) would pass CI unnoticed.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Coverage gap: large-curve encode/decode paths of the new AuthzClientCryptoProvider are untested.
raw_findings.impact: The truncation branch of integerToBytes (qLength < bytes.length) and full-size 384/521-bit r/s handling in the new ASN.1 code are never exercised; a defect specific to large-curve signatures (e.g. the ES512 66-byte length or long-form DER lengths) would pass CI unnoticed.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test fixture uses one default-curve key for all three ECDSA signature-length variants.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Initialize the KeyPairGenerator per algorithm with the matching ECGenParameterSpec (secp256r1, secp384r1, secp521r1) inside test(ECDSAAlgorithm) instead of a single default-curve key.
raw_findings.title: ES384/ES512 tests use a default P-256 key instead of curves matching the algorithm
raw_findings.trigger: testES384 and testES512 run with a single key from the JDK-default EC curve (typically secp256r1), so r/s values are always ~256-bit while len is 48 or 66.

raw_findings.body: Any bug that is symmetric between concatenatedRSToASN1DER and asn1derToConcatenatedRS (e.g. wrong tag, wrong length encoding, swapped r/s) would round-trip consistently and pass, even though the produced DER would be rejected by the JCA verifier at runtime.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Symmetric encode/decode defects in the new ASN.1 implementation would go undetected by CI.
raw_findings.impact: Any bug that is symmetric between concatenatedRSToASN1DER and asn1derToConcatenatedRS (e.g. wrong tag, wrong length encoding, swapped r/s) would round-trip consistently and pass, even though the produced DER would be rejected by the JCA verifier at runtime.
raw_findings.root_cause: The test asserts only self-consistency of the new encoder/decoder pair rather than correctness against a known-good reference.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Also assert `Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)` (DER is canonical) or verify `asn1Des` with `signature.verify(...)` against the original data.
raw_findings.title: Round-trip-only assertion never validates encoder output against the JCA-produced DER signature
raw_findings.trigger: test() only compares the concatenated form before and after re-encoding; the intermediate DER `asn1Des` is never compared to the original JCA signature `sign` nor verified with Signature.verify.

validated_findings.trigger: testES384 and testES512 run with a single key from the JDK-default EC curve (typically secp256r1), so r/s values are always ~256-bit while len is 48 or 66.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 42 shows `keyPair = KeyPairGenerator.getInstance("EC").genKeyPair();` in constructor, creating one key for all tests. The JDK default EC curve is typically secp256r1 (256-bit). Tests testES384 and testES512 use this same key with algorithm.getSignatureLength() of 96 and 132 respectively, but the actual signature r/s values remain ~256-bit. This means the truncation/padding branches for larger curves are never exercised.

validated_findings.body: Any bug that is symmetric between concatenatedRSToASN1DER and asn1derToConcatenatedRS (e.g. wrong tag, wrong length encoding, swapped r/s) would round-trip consistently and pass, even though the produced DER would be rejected by the JCA verifier at runtime.
validated_findings.failure_mode: Symmetric encode/decode defects in the new ASN.1 implementation would go undetected by CI.
validated_findings.impact: Any bug that is symmetric between concatenatedRSToASN1DER and asn1derToConcatenatedRS (e.g. wrong tag, wrong length encoding, swapped r/s) would round-trip consistently and pass, even though the produced DER would be rejected by the JCA verifier at runtime.
validated_findings.root_cause: The test asserts only self-consistency of the new encoder/decoder pair rather than correctness against a known-good reference.
validated_findings.suggested_fix: Also assert `Assert.assertArrayEquals(sign, asn1Des)` (DER is canonical) or verify `asn1Des` with `signature.verify(...)` against the original data.
validated_findings.title: Round-trip-only assertion never validates encoder output against the JCA-produced DER signature
validated_findings.trigger: test() only compares the concatenated form before and after re-encoding; the intermediate DER `asn1Des` is never compared to the original JCA signature `sign` nor verified with Signature.verify.
validated_findings.verifier_reason: Patch line 56 shows `Assert.assertArrayEquals(rsConcat, rsConcat2);` - the test only verifies round-trip consistency of the new encoder/decoder. The intermediate DER `asn1Des` is never compared to the original JCA signature `sign` nor verified with Signature.verify(). Symmetric bugs (e.g., wrong tag encoding) would pass this test but fail at runtime with actual JCA verification.
